screenSummary.playArea: A Michelson interferometer on an optical table. Light from the source is split in two by a beam splitter, sent to a movable mirror and a fixed mirror, and recombined onto a detector screen where it forms fringes.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the light source picker, the movable mirror's coarse and micrometer controls, mirror alignment, a gas cell, and a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Change the movable mirror position to sweep the fringes, or switch the source to see how coherence length limits the path difference.

michelson.patternUniform: a single fringe filling the whole field
michelson.visibilityCurve: A curve of fringe visibility against optical path difference. The visibility is {{visibility}} at the current path difference of {{pathDifference}}, and the source's coherence length is {{coherenceLength}}.

screenSummary.playArea: A Mach-Zehnder interferometer. A beam splitter sends light along two separate paths, two mirrors fold them back together, and a second beam splitter recombines them into two output ports, each with its own detector.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the light source picker, the path imbalance and mirror tilt controls, an insertable sample slide, a choice between a continuous beam and single photons, and a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Change the path imbalance and watch the light move from one port to the other, or tilt a mirror to spread the pattern into fringes.

machZehnder.currentDetails: The optical path difference is {{pathDifference}}. Port A receives {{portA}} of the light and port B receives {{portB}}. {{modeDetail}}

machZehnder.whichPathDetail: The which-path marker is on, so the two paths no longer interfere.
machZehnder.profileComplementary: The two ports are in antiphase, and their sum is the same everywhere.

screenSummary.playArea: A Fabry-Pérot interferometer. Light enters a cavity between two partly reflecting mirrors and bounces back and forth many times before leaving, so many beams interfere at once and the transmitted rings are far sharper than two-beam fringes.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the source wavelength and an optional second line, the cavity's mirror reflectance, absorption and spacing, and a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Raise the mirror reflectance and watch the broad rings narrow into sharp peaks.
